correctness.rationale: The reversible measure mu=(a/d,1,M,1,b/d) yields edge conductances (a,1,1,b) and a connected weighted path with simple spectrum. A surface-supported zero-mean Rayleigh test proves the first positive eigenvalue lies strictly below desorption rate d. Exact surface elimination gives secular F(lambda,P) with P=ab; for its first positive simple root F_lambda>0 because F(0)=0 and F_lambda(0)=-(M+2+B/d)<0. The antisymmetric one-node balanced eigenvector gives ell explicitly; at M=2/ell an eigenvector with one node persists for every split. Away from this critical M, implicit differentiation has sign -(2-M lambda) and a crossing of 2-M lambda=0 would force M=2/ell, impossible. Thus global strict monotonicity switches orientation once. The independent five-by-five generalized eigenproblem and secular comparisons passed 4,106 numerical comparisons and a symbolic determinant-factorization check, including six all-allocation critical plateaus; these are checks, not proof of the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The claim is the sharp three-regime fixed-total-rate spectral-gap allocation classification of a reversible five-state adsorption chain, with an exact central-capacity iso-gap surface. Literature establishes the wall adsorption/desorption mechanism, sticky boundary Markov approximations, and general Jacobi-eigenvalue sensitivity. The explicit fixed-sum model-specific reversal/plateau was not observed in inspected full-text sources or accessible indexed excerpts. General derivative results do not state or immediately evaluate the opposite-sign endpoint perturbation; the exact plateau is an additional algebraic degeneracy. value.rationale: A fixed total physical surface adsorption budget with reversible desorption raises a natural design question: which allocation produces the fastest L² return to equilibrium? The answer changes sharply when a central storage compartment grows, and at one exactly computable storage mass *every* allocation has the same relaxation gap despite different equilibrium surface occupancies. The necessary-and-sufficient global phase diagram and its complete critical plateau provide a substantive boundary/identifiability phenomenon, not a routine numerical example, already-tabulated computation, or arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem does not claim continuum or experimental generality.
